chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about al-Nabeez, so he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited wine in its essence, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited from the drinks every intoxicant.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A traditional fermented drink made from raisins or dates
key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine/grape wine, often used as the primary example of intoxicant

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Nabeez and how does it relate to the prohibition of wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the Quranic prohibition of 'Khamr' (wine) and the Prophetic extension of that ban to all intoxicants, a principle known as 'Kullu muskinin haram'. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential method of deriving rulings through the complementary authority of the Prophet's Sunnah, ensuring that any beverage causing intoxication is rendered unlawful regardless of its specific name or origin.
